paper_title: The Role of Model Architecture and Scale in Predicting Molecular   Properties Insights from Fine-Tuning RoBERTa, BART, and LLaMA
caption: Training Loss vs. Steps for Each Model Type by Model Size with a Data Size of 20 millions. The loss trends for 10 million and 20 million datasets are similar.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the training loss versus steps for different model types and sizes with a data size of 20 million, with the x-axis labeled "Step" and ranging from 0 to 440k on a linear scale with tick labels at 0k, 20k, 40k, 60k, 80k, 420k, 430k, and 440k, and the y-axis labeled "Train Loss" and ranging from 0.0 to 0.85 on a linear scale with tick labels at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.75, and 0.85. The plot displays six lines representing different models, including ChemBART Small 20M, ChemBART Medium 20M, ChemBERTa Small 20M, ChemBERTa Medium 20M, ChemLLaMA Small 20M, and ChemLLaMA Medium 20M, with distinct colors and solid line styles, all starting at a high training loss value around 0.8 and decreasing rapidly to around 0.1-0.2 by 80k steps, with the ChemBERTa Small 20M model (green line) showing the highest training loss at around 0.15, while the ChemLLaMA Medium 20M model (brown line) shows the lowest training loss at around 0.05, and all models continuing to decrease gradually until 440k steps.
